verdicts.reason: Verified by counting the actual file. digital-goods-marketplace-index.md:44 claims '11 confirmed pairs, 5 rejected pairs, 9 cross-cuts escalated to the global CX, 11 not-product concerns routed out'. digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md has 27 '### CX-NN' detail sections and 27 '| CX-NN |' map rows (grep -c both return 27), 7 rejected rows R-01..R-07 (cx.md:528-534), 10 escalated rows under '## Cross-Cuts Escalated to the Global CX' (cx.md:544-553, AI Provenance through Statutory Withdrawal-Waiver Gate), and 13 rows under '## Not-Product Concerns Routed Out' (cx.md:561-573, licence-key crypto through chargeback/dispute-network). All four numbers in the index are wrong and all four understate. Not blocking - no behaviour is invented - but the domain index is the navigational entry point downstream workflows read first, and it materially misdescribes its own CX file.

The quoted Role Lens sentence exists (14.01.01:27) but the question it allegedly leaves open is answered explicitly by the owning feature. 14.01.02-format-os-daw-compatibility-matrix.md:19 gives the Musician 'Read-only as buyer - Config as vendor' and states 'As vendor of a sample pack, the matrix is thin ... the required fields must collapse by product type', and 14.01.02:31 Happy Path step 1 states 'Vendor selects product type; the matrix form renders only the axes that apply to that type.' The required-sections table (14.01.01:53) is keyed to product type, not persona, and 14.01.01:99 gates publish 'for the types that require them'. So a Musician selling a preset-pack is shown the host-axes form and publish is gated - stated in three places. 'Never sees a support matrix (D-02)' is prose about the OS/CPU/architecture support matrix an executable carries (the phrase 'support matrix' is used in exactly that sense at 14.01-catalog-compatibility-cx.md:21), cited to the per-type-schema decision. No implementer builds a persona-keyed gate when every normative statement is type-keyed.

Quotes verified verbatim: 14.01-catalog-compatibility-cx.md:37, :59 and :90 all carry '[PENDING - /ideate-discover Step 5 deepening]', and ideation-index.md:65-66 record Step 5 as complete ('Must features at [DEEP] | 195 / 195 - Step 5 complete'). Not a valid tracked deferral: the markers carry no owner and their target stage is closed, so no downstream workflow picks them up. The tracking is malformed rather than absent, which is exactly the exclusion the deferral test carves out. The tree's own remediation convention proves the point - 14.01.04:56, 14.01.01:220, 14.01.01:224, 14.01.03:95 and 14.01.03:97 all carry 'Deferral re-pointed from the completed /ideate-discover Step 5 (or /ideate-validate) to ...' with an owner and a live stage; these three rows were missed. Downgraded in weight: CX-04's row (:90) is a Medium-confidence entry whose synthesis is deliberately deferred with a stated reason, and the CX-01 q5 consequence is partly priced by 14.09.02 D-02 (unconditional refund on a false verdict). The residual - the snapshot moment of a verdict relative to the waiver gate - is genuinely unowned.

All three quotes verified verbatim (14.02.03:63, 14.02.04:52, 14.02-licensing-activation-entitlement-cx.md:109), as is 14.02.01:165's 'flagged for Step 6 synthesis'. Both target stages are recorded complete (ideation-index.md:65 Step 5, :76 Step 6). Checked the exclusion: neither substantive case is covered by any tracked Open Question. 14.02.03's Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 cover reseller status, bridged refundability (resolved) and whether offline activation exists - none covers a third-party DRM account belonging to someone other than the buyer. 14.02.04's Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 cover adjudication authority, a grace window and leaked-serial detection - none covers a chargeback that was itself card fraud against the buyer. The sub-domain index's Q-01/Q-02/Q-03 cover the activation server, GDPR erasure and person-vs-org. So two product questions with real consequences (an undeclared transfer bypassing 14.06; blacklisting a theft victim) sit behind markers with no owner and a closed stage. The CX-05 role-scoping half is weaker - CX-05's synthesis is explicitly deferred on a live contingency (14.02.03 Q-01) - which is why this stays a warning.

Quotes are accurate but the claimed gaps are filled by the owning feature. (a) 'No state-machine entry': false - 14.02.01:135 states the 'active' state's trigger as 'Capture confirmed, or grant issued', which covers a minted self-entitlement. (b) 'Third kind of entitlement': not established. 14.02.01 D-06 defines the grant path as any non-purchase issuance recording grantor and reason; the ':112 enumeration' the finding cites is an edge-case row listing examples ('Freeware / NFR / promo / prize'), not a closed enum, and D-06's own context text lists NFR/educational/promo/prize as instances. A zero-price self-mint is the grant path. (c) 'No stated interaction with one-per-product-per-holder': D-07's 'One entitlement per product per holder, always' is precisely the rule that settles the coexistence case - a vendor who already self-purchased has an entitlement, so the placement binds to it rather than minting a second; 14.02.05 edge case 23 says it is minted 'at first placement ... so the chain closes', i.e. only where none exists. (d) Self-purchase flagging: 14.02.01 D-11 keys off a principal comparison ('holder principal == the product's vendor principal'), not an origin value, so it applies mechanically. (e) The origin enum literal is a data-model detail for a later layer.

verdicts.reason: Every quote is verbatim, but the divergence is neither silent nor load-bearing. 14.03.01 owns delivery and specifies the number in a parameters table, not just a decision: 14.03.01:76 'Grant window | 72 hours from mint, resumable throughout' plus ':77 Re-authorisation | Every range request', and five edge cases (E-01, E-02, E-03, E-15, E-25, E-28) all build on the 72 h grant. D-04 itself names the phrasing it supersedes ('Refines CX-01's short-lived URL phrasing') - an explicitly reconciled refinement, which is the opposite of a silent contradiction. The three counter-quotes are non-owning references that defer to 14.03.01 by citation: 14.03.03:115 says 'via a short-lived buyer-scoped URL (14.03.01 D-01). There are no static links' - the operative content there is per-request authorisation and non-static, both of which D-04 preserves ('re-authorised on every range request'), and :137 'hands off to delivery (14.03.01)'. A 72 h expiring grant is not 'a static link'; the adjective is stale, the mechanism is not contradicted. No implementer takes an adjective in a downstream consumer over a numeric parameter table and six edge cases in the owning feature. Downgraded from blocking - the two statements can both hold.

verdicts.reason: Verified literally. 14.01.01:40 locks the enum: 'The types are `plugin` - `sample-pack` - `preset-pack` - `template` - `beat`. Type is chosen first and is immutable after first publish (D-03)', and D-02 (14.01.01:206) makes the per-type value the selector for the required-section schema. 14.04.03:27 states 'A template is a listing (14.01.01) of product type `project-template`' - a different literal, asserted as fact rather than as prose. A repo-wide grep confirms this is the single divergent value: 14.04.01:34 uses `sample-pack`, 14.04.02:27 uses `preset-pack`, 14.05.01:26 uses `beat`, and `project-template` appears as an enum value nowhere else. Two normative statements about one locked, load-bearing identifier cannot both hold. Warning rather than blocking: 14.04.03 cites 14.01.01 in the same sentence, so the owner is discoverable and the referent unambiguous - but a BE spec writer extracting the enum from 14.04.03 emits the wrong literal.

The claimed contradiction misreads two levers as one. 14.04.01 D-10's own context text performs the reconciliation the finding says is missing: '14.10.03 D-01/D-02 captures the percentage and blocks payout; that is the right lever for money and the wrong one for consent.' So D-10 does not overturn 14.10.03 D-02 - it governs a different object (permission to make the pack) from the one D-02 governs (the split percentage). 14.10.03 D-02 states 'Publish is not blocked on a split', which is true and untouched. The alleged self-contradictions dissolve on reading: 14.04.01:136-137 is 'Vendor names contributors and proposes splits ... Publish is not blocked on confirmation; payout is' - confirmation of the split; and :224 'splits block payout, attestations block publish' places a consent gate on the publish side, consistent with D-10. That 14.10.03 does not carry the use question is incompleteness in a generic splits feature, not an opposite rule. The residual corner (an unanswered - as opposed to refused - use question, and post-publish refusal) is narrow, and D-10's framing as a gate that 'asks two questions' converges on requiring an answer.
verdicts.evidence: 14.04.01-sample-loop-pack-catalog.md:289 (D-10, explicit reconciliation with 14.10.03 D-01/D-02), :136-137, :224; 14.10.03-multi-contributor-pack-splits.md:97 (D-02, scoped to 'a split')

No implementer builds a termination branch against a struck-through, bolded 'the terminate branch is closed'.

verdicts.reason: Both quotes are verbatim, but the 'jointly unsatisfiable' reading requires 'deactivation' to mean landing enforcement on the remote machine, and the tree says the opposite in two places. 14.09.03 D-02: 'Revocation reaches delivery immediately even when it cannot reach the machine' - the server-side state change is deterministic and always succeeds; only the machine's next check-in is best-effort. And the seat itself is releasable server-side without the machine: 14.02.02 D-02's self-service reclaim is required to cover offline machines (14.02.03:60 - 'Self-service reclaim (14.02.02 D-02) must cover offline machines - an offline seat with no reclaim is a permanent loss'). So settlement's deactivation leg (strip entitlement, free the seats, set revoked) completes atomically; what cannot be guaranteed is the seller's already-running copy, which 14.09.03 D-01 names as an accepted permanent residue, not a settlement failure. 14.06.02's own adjacent edge case confirms the seat reading: 'Seller's machines are still activated at transfer | The buyer gets a licence with 0 free seats'. Neither statement is falsified and no transfer rolls back forever. Downgraded from blocking.

The markers exist as quoted (14.06.02:55, 14.06-used-licence-transfer-cx.md:73), but the finding's stated stake is #010 ('the one that makes its settlement contract unsatisfiable'), and that premise is refuted: the offline-machine case is answered by 14.09.03 D-01 ('Revoked-but-running is a real, permanent, accepted state') and D-02 (revocation reaches delivery regardless), with the seat freed server-side per 14.02.02 D-02 / 14.02.03:60. So the row is a stale marker over a question the tree has already answered, not an unowned behavioural gap. The second item is weaker still: 14.06-used-licence-transfer-cx.md:73 sits in CX-03, whose synthesis is deferred with an explicit stated rationale two lines below ('Deferred - Medium confidence; per-vendor variation is unmapped and the registry's shape depends on it'), which is a reasoned deferral rather than an abandoned one. The unit's substantive opens do carry owners and live stages (14.06.02 Q-01/Q-02/Q-03, 14.06.01:60 -> /create-prd), so the unit is not untracked.

The forced invention is answered verbatim by a file the finding itself cites. 14.03.03:175: 'Chargeback lands weeks after issuance | Row -> `revoked`, reason "payment reversed". The appeal route is the payment dispute, not our appeals process - routing them to us would be a dead end | "Revoked - payment reversed on {date}" + link to the payment dispute.' That is exactly the reason/trigger pair and the appeal routing the finding says must be invented. The rest is specified too: 14.02.01:138 lists chargeback as a `revoked` trigger in the state machine; 14.02.01:200 (D-10) is the normative rule; domain CX-19 (digital-goods-marketplace-cx.md:366-378) carries the full synthesis - trigger chain (chargeback -> revoked/reversed -> compensating reversal into the contributor pool per CX-21), permission intersection, notification fan-out to buyer/vendor/contributors, and the post-transfer state race; 14.09.02:185 and :217 route the case to 24.04 and mark the refund case superseded. 14.09.03's 'three triggers' sentence is a stale enumeration in one file, flagged in two places (14.02.01:179, CX-19), against behaviour that is fully determined elsewhere.
